summary: MODIS and VIIRS, two NASA satellite instruments, count fire differently, so 25 years of fire records jump in 2012 even though fire didn't. The Fire Clock merges them into one consistent record and turns it into an interactive burning calendar for any area you choose. It shows when an area bunrs, which months and years were unusual, and whether this month is normal or dangerously high. Tested on 3.36 million real detections over Punjab, it predicts hidden years within 5%. With Listen mode, Urdu and Hindi, anyone can use it.
details:
What it does
Pick any area (draw a box or type coordinates) and see 25 years of fire at a glance:

  • The Fire Clock: one ring per year, one segment per week
  • Burning calendar: month by year, with anomalies outlined
  • Early warning: is this month normal, unusually low or dangerously high?
  • Findings with confidence levels, plus CSV, chart and briefing downloads

How it works
MODIS and VIIRS count fire differently, so raw records jump in 2012. We merge MODIS Terra and Aqua, VIIRS Suomi NPP and NOAA-20 into one record by calibrating on the years they overlapped, then test it two ways: hiding years and predicting them, plus an independent physics check using fire radiative power.


Real results (Punjab, 3.36 million NASA detections)

  • Hidden years predicted within ~5%; both methods agree within 5%
  • Reproduces the 2016 peak behind Delhi’s smog crisis
  • 2025 burned 49% less than a typical year

Impact
MODIS is retiring. The Fire Clock keeps its 25-year record usable, so a fire today can be compared fairly with one from 2005.

Built for everyone
Colorblind palettes, high contrast, read-aloud, Urdu and Hindi, and Listen mode, which turns fire data into sound so blind users can explore it. A low-vision tester said: “Very good. I can’t read these fancy things, and this is good.”

Tools
HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python (pandas), GitHub Pages. Code written with AI assistance (Claude), disclosed below.
